question.text: One mole of the octahedral complex compound $\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}_3$ gives 3 moles of ions on dissolution in water. One mole of the same complex reacts with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution to yield two moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}_{(\mathrm{s})}$. The structure of the complex is:

solution.text: $\begin{array}{l}{\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \underbrace{\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right]^{2+}(\text { aq. })+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\text {aq. })}_{3 \text { ions in water }}} \\ {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2(\text { aq. })+2 \mathrm{AgNO}_3(\text { aq. }) \rightarrow} {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right]\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2(\text { aq. })+2 \mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})}\end{array}$
